clue.text: To aim at stumps encouraged, but one's not straight

parts.note: in cricket the bowler aims the ball at the stumps, so to aim at them is to bowl
egged on means urged or encouraged

explanation.surface: A cricket captain urges his bowler to attack the stumps, though the bowler's delivery is crooked.
explanation.walkthrough: CRICKET: the stumps are the three upright sticks a bowler aims at.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bandy-legged has legs that curve outwards, so their limbs are not straight.

clue.text: Travel in boat that capsizes: that's not real

indicators.note: a capsized boat is upside down, so in this down clue the built letters are read backwards
Travel is placed inside the word for boat

parts.note: a sub is a submarine, a kind of boat
to go is to travel

explanation.surface: A voyage in an overturned boat sounds too far-fetched to be true.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the capsized boat is turned upside down, so 'that capsizes' gives SGOUB read from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bogus is fake or counterfeit, the opposite of genuine.

clue.text: My motivation apparent in time?

parts.note: a whimsical reading imagines a clock explaining what drives its ticking, while the phrase is the idiom for one's inner motivation

explanation.surface: A person wonders whether their true drives will become clear eventually.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for whatever drives or motivates a person, playfully pinned on a clock's mechanism.

clue.text: Tragic scene of evil, in oriental tradition

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for east, so oriental

indicators.note: evil is put inside the word for tradition

parts.note: lore is traditional knowledge
sin is evil-doing

explanation.surface: A remark about the site of some sinister deed set in Eastern custom.
explanation.walkthrough: Elsinore is the Danish castle where Shakespeare's Hamlet is set.
explanation.definitionFit: The castle of Elsinore is the setting of Hamlet, Shakespeare's tragedy.

clue.text: Gets moving with range of signals

indicators.note: letters that move about change places, so the word Gets is rearranged

parts.note: the Urals are a Russian mountain range

explanation.surface: Someone becomes animated, using a whole repertoire of hand signals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' scrambles GETS into GEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Gestural describes communication by gestures, that is by bodily signals.

clue.text: Humble estate? I'll say

indicators.note: a speaker announcing they will say something marks a word heard spoken

parts.note: a demesne is land or an estate held by a lord

explanation.surface: Someone sarcastically calls a grand property modest, then insists on speaking up.
explanation.walkthrough: DEMESNE (a lord's estate) is pronounced like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To demean someone is to lower or humiliate them, a verb sense of humble.

clue.text: Note about absent Scottish nobleman

indicators.note: the note's letters go round the Scots word

parts.note: NB, nota bene, is a written note
awa is Scots for away, absent

explanation.surface: A memo concerns a Highland lord who is not at home.
explanation.walkthrough: A nawab was a Muslim nobleman or provincial governor in India.
explanation.definitionFit: A nawab was an Indian Muslim prince or governor, a nobleman of the Mughal era.

clue.text: No end of row about bishop who was nasty to Fanny

indicators.note: the shortened word goes round the bishop's letters
the word for row loses its last letter

parts.note: a row is a din or noise
RR, Right Reverend, is a bishop's title

explanation.surface: A churchman in endless disputes was cruel to a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No end of' leaves NOIS. Mrs Norris torments her niece Fanny Price in Jane Austen's Mansfield Park.
explanation.definitionFit: Mrs Norris is Fanny Price's spiteful aunt in Jane Austen's novel Mansfield Park.

clue.text: Guard decline to seize flier for programme not meant for unaccompanied children

definitions.text: programme not meant for unaccompanied children

parts.note: to watch is to keep guard

indicators.note: the word for decline grabs the flier, holding it inside

parts.note: to wither is to decline or fade
a moth is a flying insect

explanation.surface: A sentry's strength fades as he grabs at an insect, near a children's television show.
explanation.walkthrough: Watch With Mother was a BBC children's TV slot meant to be viewed with a parent.
explanation.definitionFit: The BBC strand's title told small children to view it alongside a parent, not on their own.

clue.text: Clearer message from Pope: achieve nothing without love

parts.note: a bull is a papal edict

indicators.note: the zero for love is dropped from the phrase

parts.note: to do zero is to achieve nothing
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: A papal pronouncement urges people to give up loving and do nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: DO ZERO without one O gives DOZER.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulldozer clears ground, so it is a clearer of land.

clue.text: They make girls unattractive to Parker: are they full of alcohol?

definitions.text: They make girls unattractive to Parker
definitions.meaning: Dorothy Parker's quip says men seldom make passes at girls who wear spectacles
drinking vessels such as tumblers are often filled with wine or spirits

explanation.definitionFit: Spectacles and drinking vessels share one word, and Parker's couplet supplies the first.

clue.text: Spoil almost everything to do with life together

parts.note: to mar is to spoil

indicators.note: the phrase for everything loses its last letter

parts.note: it all means everything

explanation.surface: A complaint that someone nearly ruins every aspect of a shared life.
explanation.walkthrough: IT ALL less its final L gives ITAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Marital means relating to marriage, the shared life of a couple.

clue.text: Pass, losing place — he says it's a game

indicators.note: the abbreviation for place is removed from the pass

parts.note: the Simplon is an Alpine pass between Switzerland and Italy

explanation.surface: Someone forgoes their turn and gives up their spot, claiming it is all just play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Simon says' is a children's game where only orders prefixed by that phrase are obeyed.
explanation.definitionFit: In the children's game, players must obey commands only when the leader prefixes them with this name and says.

clue.text: In revolt as I hand out text in Sanskrit

parts.note: people up in arms are in revolt, so up

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: During an uprising someone distributes an ancient Indian scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges ASIHAND into ANISHAD. The Upanishads are Hindu philosophical texts.
explanation.definitionFit: The Upanishads are ancient Hindu philosophical scriptures written in Sanskrit.

clue.text: One laying out black person in battle

parts.note: an inker applies ink, laying out black
a man is a person

explanation.surface: An undertaker lays out a dead soldier in a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laying out' suggests preparing a corpse, but it is spreading ink. Inkerman was a Crimean War battle of 1854.
explanation.definitionFit: Inkerman was an 1854 battle of the Crimean War between Russia and the allies.

clue.text: Wickedly suggest valuable notes are pocketed

indicators.note: the notes are put away inside the word for suggest

parts.note: to imply is to suggest
IOUs are notes promising money

explanation.surface: Someone sinisterly hints that banknotes have been stolen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' looks like music, but IOUs are promissory notes, here 'valuable' ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Impiously means without reverence for God, so in a wicked or sinful way.

clue.text: Symphony Hall in Zurich not complete

indicators.note: only part of the words is used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A concert hall in a Swiss city is still unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: Mozart's Symphony No 36 is called the Linz.
explanation.definitionFit: Mozart's Symphony No 36 is known by the name of the Austrian city.

clue.text: Happen to meet Miss Davis? Not what gentlemen would choose

indicators.note: the word for happen is placed where it meets the actress's name from within

parts.note: Bette Davis was a Hollywood actress
to run across is to happen upon

explanation.surface: A chance encounter with a Hollywood star whom polite men would not pick.
explanation.walkthrough: The title Gentlemen Prefer Blondes makes a dark-haired woman the one gentlemen would not choose.
explanation.definitionFit: Since gentlemen prefer blondes, the dark-haired alternative is what they would not pick.

clue.text: Architect's vehicle builder emptied — disgusting!

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

indicators.note: the word builder loses its inside, keeping its first and last letters

parts.note: ugh is an exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: An architect's van belonged to a builder who cleared out, and it is revolting.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir John Vanbrugh designed Blenheim Palace and Castle Howard.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John Vanbrugh was an English Baroque architect, designer of Blenheim Palace.

clue.text: After a job

definitions.meaning: the prefix meaning later or after, as in postwar

explanation.definitionFit: The prefix means following in time, and the noun is a paid position.

clue.text: One using a text from Ecclesiastes?

definitions.text: One using a text from Ecclesiastes?

parts.words: One using a text from Ecclesiastes?
parts.note: a sermon-giver takes a biblical text, and the author of Ecclesiastes is himself called by that title

explanation.surface: A minister bases a sermon on a verse from the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister delivering a sermon takes a text, and Ecclesiastes's narrator bears the same title.

clue.text: Boy is missing in Sardinia resort

indicators.note: to resort is to sort again, so the letters are rearranged once the others are taken away

explanation.surface: A lad goes missing at an Italian island holiday spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' removes I and S from SARDINIA, and 'resort' rearranges the rest, ARDINA.
explanation.definitionFit: Adrian is a boy's given name.

clue.text: Composer needs map to go over city

indicators.note: in a down clue going over means going upwards, read backwards

parts.note: Alban Berg was an Austrian composer
an A-Z is a street map

explanation.surface: A musician needs a street plan to find his way across town.
explanation.walkthrough: BERG + AZ read upwards. Zagreb is the capital of Croatia.
explanation.definitionFit: Zagreb is the capital city of Croatia.

clue.text: Depicted with undue enthusiasm, in red

definitions.meaning: a bank account in the red has more taken out than paid in

explanation.definitionFit: Exaggerated in depiction, and also describing an account that is in debit at the bank.

clue.text: Book accommodation that's cleaner

parts.note: room means space or lodging

explanation.surface: Someone reserves lodgings that a cleaner occupies.
explanation.definitionFit: A broom is a sweeping tool, a cleaning implement.

clue.text: Bike was blue

explanation.definitionFit: A small motorised cycle, and also the past tense of a verb for sulking gloomily.

clue.text: Hotter? Odds against colder

parts.note: SP, starting price, is the odds at the start of a race
icier means colder

explanation.surface: A bookmaker's question about temperature and the odds against it turning cold.
explanation.walkthrough: SP is horse racing's starting price.
explanation.definitionFit: Spicier food is hotter on the tongue, more fiery to taste.

clue.text: Sheep that hurt inside improve a bit

indicators.note: the cry of pain is put within the word for sheep

parts.note: a tup is a ram
ouch is what you say when something hurts

explanation.surface: A ram in pain is patched up slightly.
explanation.walkthrough: TUP is a ram in British farming usage.
explanation.definitionFit: To touch up is to make small improvements, a little retouching.

clue.text: Our land in that mineral-rich area

indicators.note: Britain's letters go inside the old word for that

parts.note: yon is an old word for that
for a British setter, our land is the UK

explanation.surface: A British setter speaks of their country lying in some resource-laden territory.
explanation.walkthrough: Yukon is a Canadian territory known for the Klondike gold rush.
explanation.definitionFit: Yukon, the Canadian territory, is famous for gold and other minerals.

clue.text: Rattled, lost fluid, needing anaesthetic injection

indicators.note: the anaesthetic is injected, put inside the other word

parts.note: bled means lost blood
ether was an early anaesthetic

explanation.surface: A shaken patient who has lost blood needs a jab of painkiller.
explanation.walkthrough: Rattled here means chattered on; blether is Scots for prattle.
explanation.definitionFit: To blether is to talk on foolishly, so rattled in the sense of chattered.
